findings.title: @joyrhodes2084
findings.snippet: We just returned from the Paradisus Palma Real Punta Cana (July 2025).  The best parts of our trip were certainly the service, the rooms and grounds and the community there.  The people there from the receptionists, bar tenders, our butler, Christian, the activity directors, etc. were enthusiastic, caring, friendly, personable and overly helpful.  The room and the grounds were beautiful, clean, and sufficient.  Punta Cana is beautiful:  the views, the water, the buildings, the pools, etc. We stayed in a Master Room with a swim up pool and our friends stayed in the Reserve.  Having a pool right outside our door was fantastic.  The large main pool with the swim up bar was wonderful.  There were enough free activities (A foam pool party, balloon games, daily water aerobics, Virtual Reality games, hat painting, pool pole dancing, pool trampoline exercise, nighly music in the restaurant square, etc.) to keep us busy, but not too many to make us feel like we didn't have a restful vacation.  All of the food was meh; we tried all of the restaurants.  I am not exaggerating.  Room service, however, was great.  We ordered breakfast, lunch and sometimes dinner.  We did go on two excursions:  Soana Island and a snorkeling trip. Soana island was a long day.  It was gorgeous, but the snorkeling there was lackluster and the food on the island was mediocre.  The snorkeling trip was ok; the seaweed covered most of what we were supposed to see. Overall, it was a great vacation.  We have previously stayed at the Paradisus Cancun (which was lovely with good food).

findings.title: @cindymaulick3022
findings.snippet: We love this resort and the people! We have there 14 times and are treated like family. Your review is accurate. Not much nightlife but keep in mind that it is a golf resort and SPA. Food, as vegetarians, is alright. But you can't beat the vibe, the beautiful resort itself, the other guests and especially the staff! We have made many friends, some we see year after year. This is our home away from home! PS. we do go thru a third party and pay just over $200 per night for Adults Only. Can't wait to return.

findings.title: @StephiePpn
findings.snippet:
We stayed at the Paradisus a couple years before Renos. I would miss the buffet/bar directly on the beach at night. That was so lively and fun. Our room was lovely, very very similar to yours just a little less modern, but it was still very nice and maintained just fine. The organically shaped pools and having the squiggly pool entrance attached to the buffet was amazing. Had the best massage of my life in a cabana on the beach. We had an amazing time except for a couple small things. The biggest thing was all the difficulty we had making dinner reservations. Despite that we really looked forward to going back until it closed for Reno’s :(. 

Two questions. 1) is there any type of reservation system now to avoid miscommunication?

2) 10th anniversary. Do you reccommend this or Lopesan?

findings.title: @cindymaulick3022
findings.snippet:
I guess a golf resort and spa screams nightlife to some, hard rock implies that to me personally. Golf and spa invoke relaxation to me.
Food is OK, if you expect NYC 5 star status you won't find it there. 
As for the staff, they do the best they can. They work long hours for very little money.
We are going back in a few weeks for our 15th time to celebrate our anniversary. Wouldn't go anywhere else, love this place and the wonderful Dominican people. 
As for communicating with locals, use a translator app, they have guests from all over the globe so you can't expect them to know your language. You give respect, you will get it back

findings.title: @CoachPattyBlueHayes
findings.snippet:
The place looks wonderful. If you go back to the DR, I'd encourage you to consider visiting a local boys and girls club and taking a little bit of your vacation time to learn about the local living conditions for many of the locals. I was in Puerto Plata in neighborhoods where families have no running water, sewage running through the tiny streets and their homes are shacks (many taken with last year's floods) of metal or at best, cinderblock. They don't have room service - lucky to have enough to eat every day. 
You know how amazing the local people are - the kids I met have the brightest smiles and now they have educational dreams! I volunteered with Dove Missions, if you go to the north of the DR. There are great resorts there, too - and you can meet the awesome kids from Dove Missions. :-)
